body:
Credit to @Jirentian for the report (a hand-installed plugin's provider fell back to the generic glyph whatever icon name it declared).

The icon a plugin's provider wears had only two sources: the picture its auth hook (or its package.json's `magpie.icon`) gives — an https URL or a `data:image` URI, which magpie checks and keeps — and the one the plugin market lists for it, where a bare name (`deepseek-color`) goes through as it is. A plugin installed by hand that said a bare icon name was refused by both readers, so its provider fell back to the generic glyph no matter what it declared: `host.js`'s `iconOf` carried only a URL or a data URI, and `provider.pluginOwnIcon` asked `iconURL` of the value, which takes a URL. That is why so many third-party plugins showed the same plain mark.

A bare name — one with no scheme and no path in it — now passes both readers as it is, exactly as a market name does; the page already draws such a name from its bundled icons and falls back to the generic glyph for one it has no file of. A picture is still checked, fetched and kept as before, and the market fallback is untouched, so a plugin that says nothing shows what the market gives it, and one that says nothing at all keeps the generic mark.

| What | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `TestPluginSaidIconName` (new, provider): a bare name passes, a URL is still kept as a picture | fails without the fix, passes with it |
| `TestPluginOwnIconAndKeyHint` (plugin, extended): a plugin's auth hook says `deepseek-color`, it reaches the provider list as that name | fails without the fix, passes with it |
| Ablation | both fail again with only the two implementation files reverted |
| `go test -tags nogui ./internal/provider ./internal/plugin ./internal/agent` | provider and plugin green; the two failures (`TestHostToldTheGatewayAddress`, `TestMothX`) fail the same way on clean `upstream/main` (pre-existing, not touched by this patch) |
| the new test's isolation (rework after the audit) | the audit's reruns went red 3 of 3 with the test's assertions passing (0.0s) and only its TempDir removal failing ("directory not empty"). The rerun log's "leaked renewal loop" read was wrong: the writer was the test's own stub, which answered a success, so `pluginOwnIcon`'s background fetch goroutine went on after the test was over and kept the (empty) picture into the temp HOME — proved with a probe that watches `plugin-icons.json` land after the body has ended. The stub now refuses the fetch: nothing is written after the body ends, the test is green solo five times and under `-race`, and the TempDir failure has not come back in any run since |
| `go test -tags nogui -count=3 ./internal/provider` (rework) | the one failure left is `TestCodexSubagentModelsKept`, a pre-existing allocation-budget flake of the suite on this machine: it fails byte for byte the same (516096/1756568) on clean `upstream/main` under the same `-count=3`, and passes with this patch in a fully green full-suite run and in `-count=1` runs; not touched by this patch |
| `gofmt` / `go vet -tags nogui` / `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -tags nogui` | clean |

**Attribution**: AI-written; I've read the whole diff and the tests pass. Please keep the author (ggbdpq) or add Co-authored-by: ggbdpq ggbdpq@gmail.com

**Branch with the commit**: `fix/5103-provider-icon` on [ggbdpq/magpie](https://github.com/ggbdpq/magpie) (head ac22f82f3 (rebased onto current `upstream/main` with this rework folded in; `git am -3`-tested against that base)).

What this does not take on, for a maintainer's call first: a per-provider icon picked in the editor (today only a provider the user added has the picker, and a signed-in account's save drops an icon from its body), and serving a local file as one. Both grow the settings surface; this patch keeps to what a plugin already declares.
